historical_references.reference: Muizz li-Din Allah was the fifth caliph of the Fatimid Caliphate, ruling from 1110 to 1130 CE. He is known for his successful military campaigns against the Crusaders and for his patronage of scholars and architects.

The name Muizz li-Din Allah means 'helper of the faith of Allah'. It was a title used by several Islamic rulers throughout history. Another notable ruler with this title was Muizz ud-Din Muhammad Ghurid, who founded the Ghurid Empire in Afghanistan in the late 12th century CE.
